# Vertigo Tracker

> An iPhone vertigo and dizziness diary (formerly Rin Sky / めまい日記). Log a spinning, floating or lightheaded attack, or a headache, the moment it happens, and turn your records into a PDF for your doctor. Not related to "Rin: Migraine Tracker", which is a different app from a different developer.

App Store name: "Vertigo Tracker" (US) / 「めまい手帳 - 頭痛・気圧の記録と予報」 (Japan). App Store ID 6799015322. Category: Medical. It is a journal, not a medical device: it does not diagnose or predict attacks.

## What it does

- Log an attack with large buttons, no typing: headache, dizziness or both; dizziness type (spinning, floating, lightheaded, other); how long it lasted; how bad it was (3 steps: mild, moderate, severe)
- Timer: start it when an attack begins, stop it when it ends, and the duration is measured instead of remembered
- Optional details afterwards: possible triggers, accompanying symptoms (tinnitus, ear fullness, nausea, headache and more), medicines and whether they helped, notes
- Barometric pressure: the iPhone's built-in barometer is read the moment a record is saved; the pressure forecast for your area (Apple's weather service) is shown on the same timeline
- Doctor PDF for the last 30 days, 90 days or all time (a Vertigo Tracker Pro feature; a sample is always viewable); CSV export
- Records stay in a database on the device. No server, no account. The only thing that leaves the device is a rounded area used to look up the pressure forecast

## Who it is for

- People with recurring vertigo or dizziness (for example Ménière's disease, BPPV, vestibular migraine) who want an accurate record to show a doctor
- People who also have recurring headaches and want both in one log
- iPhone only (iOS 16 or later). English and Japanese

## App Store

- US: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/id6799015322
- Japan: https://apps.apple.com/jp/app/id6799015322
